summary: The gaia variant is a design + code system. It covers the main monitoring, aggregation, hotspot, notification, pest-control, administration, and resident concepts in the GAIA document and README, but the implementation has two competing runnable models and one critical unsafe parsing issue. Because the source contains eval() on received message bodies, the report recommendation is fail despite generally good conceptual coverage.

findings.description: The design explicitly models the core roles needed by the requirements: sensor nodes, central coordination, pattern recognition, notification, building administration, pest control, and student residents.
findings.evidence: gaia/System monitorowania i likwidacji infestacji karaluchowtest.pdf: role model includes SensorNode, CentralCoordinator, PatternRecognitionModule, NotificationService, BuildingAdministration, PestControlCompany, and StudentResident; gaia/implementation_workspace/README.md:7-15 lists the same components.

findings.description: The implementation defines data contracts for sensor readings, alerts, and high-activity zones with count, location, and timestamp fields.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py:12-29 defines SensorData with sensor_id, cockroach_count, location, timestamp; lines 32-47 define AlertDetails; lines 50-64 define HighActivityZone.

findings.description: The SPADE coordinator parses received message bodies with eval(), which can execute arbitrary Python if a message body is malicious or malformed.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py:127-132 receives a SensorData message and calls SensorData.from_dict(eval(msg.body)).

findings.description: The workspace contains two separate implementations of the same system, one SPADE-based and one asyncio queue-based, making it unclear which implementation is authoritative.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/README.md:27-29 says to run python main.py, while gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py:70-132 defines SPADE Agent classes and gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:67-129 defines separate non-SPADE component classes.

findings.description: The SPADE message body is serialized with str(dict) and then parsed with eval instead of a defined JSON schema or validated contract.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py:97-100 sends body=str(sensor_data.to_dict()); line 132 parses that body with eval(msg.body).

findings.description: Production paths use print statements for operational behavior and alerts rather than a logging or notification abstraction.
findings.evidence: gaia/implementation_workspace/main.py:74,91,106,113 print runtime status; gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py:77,102,115,129 print agent events.

logical_inconsistencies: The README points users to main.py, but mas_system.py implements a different SPADE-based multi-agent system with different communication mechanics.
The interface contract is not stable: the sender emits Python dict string representations and the receiver evaluates them as code instead of validating structured JSON.
implementation_risks: Critical code execution risk from eval(msg.body) in gaia/implementation_workspace/mas_system.py.
Two parallel implementations can diverge in behavior and make testing or deployment ambiguous.
Print-based alerting and status output make it hard to integrate with real notification channels, observability, or audit logs.
